Contents.Html:
[page[title]]

Own the platform SSO boundary and the lifecycle of an identity before it belongs to any individual application.

All platform domainsView the GitHub repositoryRead the documentation

What it owns

  • Authentication, sessions, tenants and SSO users.
  • Registration, invitations and password-reset flows.
  • Publishes account lifecycle events for downstream domains and supplies Web and HostedServices hosts.

Why the boundary matters

Identity is managed once at the correct trust boundary rather than copied into every business application.

How it fits

The domain is published and tested independently, then composed through cCoder.Core when an application needs the complete platform. That keeps ownership visible while preserving a straightforward application bootstrap.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in cCoder.Security on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.Security" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddSecurityApi((services, security) =>
{
    security.RootPath = "Api/Security";
    // Add the selected model and password-encryption providers here.
});

app.StartSecurityWeb();

Configure and run it

Configure the SSO persistence provider, password encryption, sessions and the API root. Use AddSecurityHostedServices and StartSecurityHostedServices when token cleanup and event processing run outside the Web host.

Consume the capability

Authenticate through the account/session boundary, then use the Security OData sets such as SSOUser, Tenant and UserEvent. Subscribe to account lifecycle events instead of copying SSO state directly.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/cCoder.Security.git
cd cCoder.Security
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
